title: Persist meeting recordings locally in IndexedDB parts, with upload as fallback
context: The input does not state the motive. The commit adds a meeting recorder that captures Chrome tab/system audio and microphone, with live meters, upload, and auto-transcribe. Its body says uploads have a 'local fallback', and the structured changes add IndexedDB helpers (idb, putSession, allSessions, putPart, partsRange). Together these point to recordings being kept on the device, but src/Recorder.js is not in the shown diff, so the write path is inferred from names.
decision: Recording audio is stored in the browser's IndexedDB, as sessions and parts, and the upload to the server is a fallback path. The recordings history, playback, rename, re-transcribe and delete work from this local store. The shown code does not confirm whether parts are written during capture or only at stop.
consequences: Recordings can survive a failed or interrupted upload, since a local copy exists.
History, playback and re-transcribe read from the browser store, so they are per-browser and per-origin.
Storage limits and cleanup now depend on the browser's IndexedDB quota, which the input does not address.
Upload and transcription logic is split between the local store and the server API in src/api.js, which now uses a same-origin base in production.
